This site is a learning project. It is a first scaffold for hearing environmental data, not a finished instrument, a validated method or expert composition. It was made by **Graham Watt** working with **Claude Code**, Anthropic's AI coding agent. The split of the work was uneven, and anyone reading, listening or reusing the code should know how.

## What Graham brought

- **The question and the curiosity.** Could a year of a river, or seventy years of an ocean, be *heard*, and would hearing it teach something a chart doesn't?
- **Domain knowledge.** Years of practice in watershed planning and flood mitigation in southern British Columbia. He chose the rivers, the records and the ecological stories worth telling: ice, freshet, drought, sockeye and storms.
- **The literature.** He built and curates the working library of several dozen papers on sonification, auditory display and data analysis behind these choices, and reviews how their findings are integrated.
- **Opinions on how data work should be done.** The rules show up throughout: every sound is tagged by whether its data were retrieved, derived or simulated; renders must repeat exactly; uncertainty and data gaps are made audible, not smoothed away; and nothing is published without an independent review first.
- **The environment the work happened in.** Graham built a personal research environment (notes, a literature library, decision logs and review workflows) that the agent works inside. That is why this project has a decision record, provenance tags and a pre-publication review.
- **Listening and direction.** He decided which pieces were keepers, what style to reach for and which data to add next.

## What Claude Code led

Graham has no training in music theory and is a beginner in Python. So the following was proposed, decided and built by Claude Code, and explained to Graham along the way:

- **The music theory:** the mode ladder, chord loops, voice leading, rhythms and orchestration.
- **Most of the data-to-sound mapping:** which variable drives which instrument, the thresholds, smoothing and hysteresis, and the balance of the mix.
- **All of the code:** the data fetching, the sampling and synthesis engine, the scores, the listening companion and this website.
- **The analysis and checks:** derived variables, the quality-check plots, and the reproducibility tests.
- **Most of the writing** on this site, including this page.

Before the first release, the code was also reviewed by another Claude model and by Google Gemini models. Their findings were checked against the code before anything was changed.

## What that means for you

- **The data are real and sourced.** Every record is credited on the Methods pages, and the scripts fetch it from the provider.
- **The musical and code choices are one reasonable first attempt**, made by an AI system under a domain expert's direction. They are interpretive, not authoritative, and a composer or a software engineer would make many of them differently.
- **It is a scaffold to grow from.** The code is open (Mozilla Public License 2.0) and meant to be read, questioned and changed. Suggestions and corrections are welcome as [issues on GitHub](https://github.com/cordilleran/sonify-viz/issues).
